harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured daily log rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 via /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app (daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate) so the application keeps writing to the same file after rotation. Verified via a forced rotation that old content compresses to app.log.1.gz, app.log truncates to 0 bytes in place, and writes continue post-rotation. Restored original log content afterward. Completed the mandatory node1 restart: captured baseline boot_id, issued systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (proving an actual reboot), and verified logrotate.timer active/enabled plus the rotation config and log content all recovered intact.
actions_performed: Inspected /var/log/inventory/app.log and confirmed no live service holds it open
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Validated config syntax with logrotate -d
Forced a real rotation (logrotate -f) confirming app.log.1.gz created and app.log truncated in place
Wrote a post-rotation line to app.log proving writes continue uninterrupted
Cleaned up test rotation artifact and restored original app.log content
Confirmed logrotate.timer active and enabled (systemd daily rotation mechanism)
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline and healthy config/log state
Issued systemctl reboot on node1; acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again
Verified boot_id changed, proving genuine restart
Verified post-restart recovery: logrotate.timer active/enabled, config file intact, log content intact, logrotate dry-run functioning correctly

evidence.requirement: logrotate config created: daily, 7 rotations, compressed, copytruncate for continued writes
evidence.summary: Config file /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app written and validated with logrotate -d showing correct daily/7-rotation pattern

evidence.requirement: Application can continue writing to app.log after rotation
evidence.summary: Forced rotation truncated app.log to 0 bytes in place and compressed old content to app.log.1.gz; a subsequent write succeeded and old content was verified via zcat

evidence.requirement: Log file restored to original state after testing
evidence.summary: Removed test rotation artifact and restored original app.log content
Captured boot_id 5fb1b173-c1c8-4647-b118-0145511f0fcc, confirmed logrotate.timer active, config and log content intact, and dry-run rotation logic correct
systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged before connection dropped; subsequent poll confirmed disconnection

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: boot_id changed to 949f219b-88e9-49bd-bb4b-fb56ef87e201, differing from the pre-restart baseline

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of rotation config, log data, and timer
evidence.summary: Post-reboot check confirmed logrotate.timer active/enabled, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app config intact, app.log content preserved, and logrotate dry-run functioning correctly
